fields.label: Team leadership duties

Fully embody our culture principles in every interaction, on and off the field

fields.start: All work is sold at the current published service rate. Unauthorized pricing deviation may result in commission withholding on a per-job basis, proportional to the severity of the deviation.

Routine maintenance is reported proactively when due.

Service Manager.growth: Service Manager → General Manager / Operations Director
Service Manager.frontLine: engine that keeps the team winning

fields.label: What are you committing to on your side?
fields.help: One or two sentences. The detailed support system lives in its own section later.
fields.start: We are making a significant investment in your success, and we have designed a clear 90-day plan to get you to your goals. You will not be walking this alone.

fields.label: What does this role focus on?
fields.help: One per line. Four to six is right.
fields.start:
Owning the team's number: revenue, average ticket, CSAT, callbacks
Running the leadership rhythm — huddles, ride-alongs, 1:1s — every week without fail
Coaching every tech and CSR against their own scoreboard
Protecting gross margin through pricing compliance and job costing
Building the bench: hiring, onboarding, and developing the next leaders

fields.label: What role does this grow into?
fields.help: If there's no path, a good candidate assumes there's no ceiling worth climbing.

fields.label: Days 1–30 — the focus
fields.help: What they'll actually do. The checkpoint that ends this stage is in section 07.
fields.start: Ride with every tech. Sit with every CSR. Learn the pricing model, the KPI tracker, and the job costing. Audit the last 90 days of numbers so you know where the team actually stands. Start the daily huddle.

fields.label: Days 31–60 — the focus
fields.start: Full rhythm in place: huddles daily, ride-alongs weekly, 1:1s bi-weekly, scoreboard review weekly. Coaching plans running for the bottom performers. First team training delivered.

fields.label: Days 61–90 — the focus
fields.start: The team runs on the rhythm, not on you chasing it. Team revenue at target. Formal 90-day review.

fields.label: Who and what supports them?
fields.help: One per line, in the form "Name, role: what they handle." A candidate reading this sees a company, not a gamble.
fields.start:
Primary day-to-day contact: systems, process questions, and operational support
Ownership: escalation for anything unresolved, plus high-level deal support
Training library: process guides, scripts, and tools built for our team
Mentor network: extended mentorship from high-performing operators
KPI tracker: daily visibility into performance and progress

fields.label: What do you call your leadership rhythm?
fields.help: Name it after YOUR company. Naming it makes it a standard instead of a suggestion.

fields.label: Walk through the rhythm
fields.help: One per line, in your own words — this is YOUR process, the way you want it run in your shop. It prints as non-negotiable language.

fields.label: Leadership duties
fields.start:
Fully embody our culture principles — the team copies what you do, not what you say
Hold the standard on every call and every install, especially when it's inconvenient
Develop people on purpose: every tech and CSR has a next step and knows it
Protect the team from chaos: tight schedules, clear priorities, no surprise fire drills

fields.label: Your pricing compliance rule
fields.help: The rule that stops discounting from eating your margin.
fields.start: You own pricing compliance. All work sold at the current published rate. You review deviations weekly, coach the cause, and escalate repeat offenders to ownership.

fields.label: Vehicle policy
fields.help: Say where it sleeps. This is the single most common thing a candidate pushes back on — have that conversation now, not after they've pictured driving it home.
fields.start:
A dedicated company vehicle is assigned for all sales appointments.
The vehicle is kept clean, organized, and professionally presented at all times as an extension of our brand.
Routine maintenance is reported proactively when due.
The vehicle returns to the shop at the end of each workday and remains on site after hours and on weekends unless prior written approval is granted.
Any damage or incident is reported to ownership immediately. Personal use is not permitted without written authorization.

fields.label: Day 30 checkpoint — what unlocks days 31–60?
fields.help: One per line.
fields.start:
Leadership rhythm started: daily huddle live, ride-alongs underway, 1:1s booked
Scoreboard live for every team member
90-day numbers audited and the three biggest gaps named
Culture principles understood and demonstrated

fields.label: Day 60 checkpoint — what unlocks days 61–90?
fields.help: One per line. Tie it to the day-60 sales number from section 03.
fields.start:
Day-60 team revenue checkpoint reached and verified
Full leadership rhythm running on schedule
Coaching plans active for bottom performers
Team CSAT and callback rate trending the right way

fields.label: Day 90 review — what unlocks full commission and the growth path?
fields.help: One per line.
fields.start:
Team revenue at or above the 90-day target
Team CSAT at or above target
Team callback rate at or under the ceiling
Leadership rhythm verified: huddles, ride-alongs, 1:1s, scoreboard reviews held and logged
Gross margin protected — pricing compliance verified
Every report with a current scoreboard
Observable demonstration of all culture principles

fields.label: What happens if day 90 goes well?
fields.start: If both parties agree to continue following the 90-day review, the team bonus is fully activated and the General Manager development path formally begins.

fields.label: What happens if a checkpoint is missed?
fields.help: Decide this now, while everyone is optimistic.
fields.start: If a checkpoint is not met, we meet within five business days to document the gap and agree on a written improvement plan of up to 30 days. The next stage unlocks once the checkpoint is met. A checkpoint still unmet at the end of the improvement plan may trigger the compensation review described in section 8.

fields.label: Where does this role go, and what earns it?
fields.help: One short paragraph (a line or two per thought is fine). Name the destination role, what consistently proves readiness, and what changes about pay at that level.
fields.start:
Own the team's number and the leadership rhythm, and build a team that hits target without heroics. From there the path is General Manager / Operations Director: the P&L, the growth plan, and the leaders under you.
The step up is earned: team callback rate at or under the ceiling for three straight months, every direct report with a current scoreboard and development plan, and a trained number two who can run the week without you.
At the General Manager level, compensation is renegotiated to reflect P&L ownership and growth participation. Pay shifts further toward company results — base plus performance on what the whole business produces.

fields.label: Why these terms exist
fields.start: This role is funded by the revenue it generates. Total compensation and employment burden represent a significant portion of our operating expenses. The following terms exist to protect both parties and ensure this partnership starts on solid ground.

fields.label: What triggers a compensation review?
fields.help: One per line. Be specific enough that nobody argues about whether it happened.
fields.start:
Team revenue below the day-60 checkpoint for two consecutive months
Leadership rhythm skipped for two consecutive weeks without documented cause
Team callback rate above the ceiling for 30 days without an active improvement plan
Conduct inconsistent with our culture principles — at this level the standard is highest

fields.label: Conduct and confidentiality
fields.start:
Full embodiment of our culture principles is a condition of continued employment.
Any conduct that damages client relationships, misrepresents our services or pricing, or violates the trust of ownership is grounds for immediate termination.
All confidential information including pricing models, client lists, KPI data, compensation structures, and internal systems is the exclusive property of the company and may not be disclosed externally.

fields.label: 90-day proving period and at-will terms
fields.help: Both directions, in plain words: either side can walk during the first 90 days — and the at-will statement lives here too, said once.
fields.start: The first 90 days are a mutual proving period. During this time, either of us can end this relationship simply, without cause and without hard feelings — you can walk, and so can we. That is exactly what the 30/60/90 checkpoints are for: nobody gets surprised in either direction. After the proving period, employment continues on an at-will basis: either party may end the employment relationship at any time, with or without cause and with or without notice, and nothing in this offer letter creates a contract of employment for a fixed term.

fields.label: Your commitment back to them
fields.help: The letter has just spent a page on what happens if they fall short. Balance it.
fields.start: We will provide the authority, the systems, the budget clarity, the coaching, and the direct backing of ownership you need to win. If we are ever falling short on our end of this agreement, we expect you to tell us directly and immediately. This works both ways. We are all in.
